acceptance_criteria.evidence: MET, and the row's own snapshot was already stale when I read it. Today's figure was RE-DERIVED BY RUN, not copied: `elixir scripts/pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs` from the repo root prints `textual  baseline  108  derived  108  ==`. acceptance_criteria.criterion: THE ARM STOPS PINNING A BUCKET COUNT AT ALL. The selftest's own header promises the opposite in as many words — 'Asserts exit codes, arm names and refusal prose — NEVER a bucket count, so an honest lens correction can never red it.' Re-pointing the arm at today's number reinstates the identical defect one wave later. Either the arm asserts what the header promises, or the header is amended to admit its one exception; silently re-pinning is refused.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: MET at THREE sites, and by derivation rather than by deletion. (a) D448-REFUSAL-IS-THE-ARM: `expect` no longer contains "baseline  104  derived  104  =="; it asserts @drift_row_injected, a module attribute built beside @rederived the way drift/4 builds the row (column padding included) from @rederived.unrouted + 1. (b) D448-BASELINE-REFUSES: its two count-bearing expectations and its `mut` anchor are derived the same way; it previously pinned "unrouted baseline 24 derived 23" and the anchor literal "unrouted: 23". (c) THE SITE NOBODY HAD FILED - api/test/barkpark/pds_elixir_census_test.exs, the CI-GATED ExUnit wrapper, shipped `@baseline_from "unrouted: " <> "23"` and `assert out =~ "unrouted baseline 24 derived 23"`, a pinned tree-derived count on the required Elixir gate, in the file whose own section 'Why the assertions are on prose, never on numbers' (:49) forbids it. Replaced by baseline_perturbation/1, which reads today's figure out of the census source and perturbs it by one. Verified mechanically: `unrouted: 24` and `baseline  104` now occur ZERO times in the census; `unrouted: 23` occurs exactly once, in @rederived itself, which is the real baseline and not an anchor. Both instruments still assert the side they INJECT and never the side the tree derives, which is what the banner asks for. || THIS CRITERION UNDER-DESCRIBES WHAT SHIPPED, AND THE GAP IS RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN EDITED INTO THE CRITERION (lead ruling, 2026-08-22; editing acceptance_criteria under my own claim would 409 my own close on the claim-time work digest). The criterion says THE ARM, singular. THREE sites shipped. The sibling D448-BASELINE-REFUSES was NOT dead-red - it was GREEN, and green only because @rederived.unrouted still happened to equal the 23 its anchor and its two count-bearing expectations were typed against. GREEN BECAUSE THE NUMBER HAS NOT MOVED YET IS NOT GREEN: on the first honest correction of `unrouted` its expectations would have failed and its `mut` anchor would have refused with MUTATION ANCHOR GONE. The third site, api/test/barkpark/pds_elixir_census_test.exs, was the same shape ON THE REQUIRED ELIXIR GATE, where the red would land on main and name a PR that never touched the census. All three are now derivation-based. An auditor reading only the criterion would credit one repair and miss the two that were still armed.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: MUTATION PROOF: with the fix in place, apply the arm's OWN `mut` pair ({"++ baseline_checks(drift_rows, classified)", "++ []"}) and confirm the case still reds for the RIGHT reason — D448's refusal not firing — rather than passing because the assertion was weakened into something unfalsifiable. An arm that no mutation can red is decoration.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: MET, and it exposed a SECOND defect the row had not seen. Applying the arm's own pair alone is precisely the state the case SHIPPED in: `mut` held ONE pair and that pair only removed the enforcement, so nothing was perturbed and NO DRIFT ROW WAS EVER PRINTED. Measured, three variants on today's tree: disarm-only -> exit 0, every row `==`, no DRIFT; move-baseline-only -> exit 1, FAIL D448-DRIFT-REFUSES; BOTH -> exit 0 with the DRIFT row printed, which is the pre-wave-47 behaviour the case exists to exhibit. So retyping 104 -> 108 would have produced a GREEN THAT PROVED NOTHING. Fix: apply_mutation/2 now takes a LIST of pairs under the same exactly-once anchor refusal, and the case carries both halves. THE MUTATION PROOF THIS CRITERION ASKS FOR, RUN: revert the case to its single-pair `mut` and the selftest reds with exactly one failure - 'FAIL  D448-REFUSAL-IS-THE-ARM  exit 0 as required but never printed ["unrouted       baseline   24  derived"]'. The assertion is therefore falsifiable and detects the exact half-mutated state. SECOND ARM, on the gated wrapper: drop `++ baseline_checks(drift_rows, classified)` from the census for real and ExUnit reports 4 tests, 1 failure - the baseline arm, 'a census whose committed population baseline no longer matches the tree exited 0'. So the derived anchor did not weaken it either.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: NEGATIVE ARM: the other 35 cases still behave as required and the run reports a clean completion (RC=0). DELETING D448-REFUSAL-IS-THE-ARM to reach exit 0 is explicitly rejected unless justified in writing — an arm removed is not an arm fixed, and this arm's stated purpose is to prove the D448 red is produced by D448 and not by a neighbouring check.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: MET. `elixir scripts/pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs --selftest` from the repo root on the final commit: 'SELFTEST OK - 36 cases, 25 of them mutants that went red as required.' RC=0, zero FAIL lines; the 35 previously-passing cases still pass and D448-REFUSAL-IS-THE-ARM joins them, so the count is 36 PASS. NO ARM WAS DELETED - the case list is longer in content, not shorter: both D448 cases are intact and both now carry a perturbation they previously did not apply. Also green alongside it: the plain census (exit 0, UNDISPOSED 0, sum 260 == population 260, PASS D448-DRIFT-REFUSES) and the gated ExUnit arms (4 tests, 0 failures, mix format --check-formatted clean).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: THE GATING GAP IS NAMED AND DISPOSED OF. This row records that `--selftest` is NOT CI-gated, which is precisely why the arm rotted dead-red for two waves without anyone noticing. State whether gating is fixed here or filed as its own row: a repaired arm that nothing runs will rot again, and the whole finding is that an instrument nobody exercises certifies nothing.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: MET by disposition, stated rather than fixed, and the row's premise turned out to be half wrong. THE GATING GAP IS A RECORDED DECISION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT: api/test/barkpark/pds_elixir_census_test.exs:32-46 already documents why `--selftest` is not gated - 'disqualified on price, not on merit' - with a metered figure and an instruction to re-read the census's own derived floor rather than quote the paragraph, and four cheap arms ride the required gate in its place. I am NOT filing a gating row and NOT adding the selftest to CI. THE REASON: the gating gap is not what rotted. The pinned count is - and the identical pinned count sat on the GATED arm, where a gate did exist, ran on every merge, and did not help, because a hardcoded number cannot detect its own staleness no matter how often it executes. Both sites are now derivation-based, so neither can rot this way whether or not anything runs them. This is offered as a disposition, not a ruling: if the lead wants a gating row anyway I will file it with the measured cost attached.

content.description:
The census's own `--selftest` exits 1 on clean origin/main (verified: worktree at origin/main, `elixir scripts/pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs --selftest` -> rc=1, "SELFTEST FAILED - 1 case(s)").

FAILING ARM: D448-REFUSAL-IS-THE-ARM, the @selftest_cases entry immediately after D448-BASELINE-REFUSES in scripts/pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs. It asserts:

    mut:    {"++ baseline_checks(drift_rows, classified)", "++ []"}
    exit:   0
    expect: ["CENSUS OK", "baseline  104  derived  104  =="]

That 104 is a HARDCODED BUCKET COUNT and it is two re-derivations stale. The textual baseline went 104 -> 106 (BPML W3 wave) -> 107 (create-on-push wave); neither wave updated the arm. No @rederived row on main equals 104, so the expectation can never match and the arm has been dead-red for two waves.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A STALE NUMBER: the selftest's own header promises the exact opposite, in as many words -- "Asserts exit codes, arm names and refusal prose - NEVER a bucket count, so an honest lens correction can never red it." This arm is the single exception that falsifies that sentence. It is the defect class the census exists to catch, living inside the census's own self-check.

WHY IT ROTTED UNNOTICED: --selftest is not CI-gated. api/test/barkpark/pds_elixir_census_test.exs documents it as "disqualified on price, not on merit" (~210s USER CPU across 33 port-child invocations), so nothing runs it on merge.

THE FIX IS NOT TO TYPE 107. Three concurrent branches legitimately hold three different values right now -- main 107, PR #9600 106 (correction/2 left the literal lens), PR #9530 108 (a new receipt site) -- which is itself the proof that pinning a count in this arm is the bug rather than the number being wrong. Either assert the arm's PROSE only (that the drift block still prints, CENSUS OK still appears, and D448-DRIFT-REFUSES is absent -- the `refute` key already carries that half), or derive the expected row from @rederived at runtime so an honest re-derivation can never red it.

PROVENANCE: found while re-deriving the census for PRs #12526, #9600 and #9530. Not caused by any of them -- reproduced identically on all three branches AND on a clean origin/main worktree, which is the control that makes this pre-existing rather than collateral.

INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED 2026-08-20 by criteria-standalone, from a different tree and without having seen this row: clean `git archive origin/main api/lib scripts` at e60f0a57b9, `elixir scripts/pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs --selftest` -> RC=1, 35 PASS / 1 FAIL, the sole failure being 'D448-REFUSAL-IS-THE-ARM  exit 0 as required but never printed ["baseline  104  derived  104  =="]'. Two readers, two trees, same verdict. Surfaced while verifying pds-w37-selftest-zero-row-floor, whose criterion 3 could NOT be stamped met because this arm reds the instrument: the KEYS half of that row is fully proven, but a selftest that exits 1 certifies nothing for anyone. Priority raised 2 -> 1 on that ground.

THE SELFTEST STATES THE RULE TWICE AND VIOLATES IT A DOZEN LINES AWAY — located by the team lead as a third reader, re-verified here at origin/main e60f0a57b9. All three sites are in scripts/pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs; ANCHOR ON THE QUOTED TEXT, the line numbers are a hint at that sha only (this file's own epic is about line anchors rotting):

  1. THE VIOLATION (~:6748), inside the D448-REFUSAL-IS-THE-ARM case:
       expect: ["CENSUS OK", "baseline  104  derived  104  =="],
     and its own `proves` explains the arm's purpose — "so the red above is produced by this
     arm and not by a neighbouring check the mutation happened to disturb". The purpose is
     sound; the hardcoded 104 is what makes it unreachable.

  2. THE RULE AS A DESIGN COMMENT (~:3669):
       "# THE COUNT-FREE DISCRIMINATOR. The selftest asserts arm names and refusal prose and
        # NEVER a bucket count, so the injection proof cannot be shipped as "expect 24" — an
        # honest register edit would red it."

  3. THE RULE AS TEXT THE CENSUS PRINTS TO THE OPERATOR (~:6760):
       p("  prose — NEVER a bucket count, so an honest lens correction can never red it.")

The printed sentence sits TWELVE LINES below the expectation that breaks it. The census tells its reader "an honest lens correction can never red me" while carrying the one arm an honest lens correction reds — a check whose PRINTED claim is stronger than what it enforces, with the violation inside the very mechanism built to prevent it.

THREE READERS, THREE TREES, ONE VERDICT: criteria-standalone and the team lead each ran a clean `git archive origin/main` extract independently and both got RC=1 with D448-REFUSAL-IS-THE-ARM as the sole failure, alongside this row's original report. The lead reached "hardcoded numbers, drift-prone shape" as a labelled HYPOTHESIS; this row supplies the cause (104 -> 106 -> 107, two waves stale, no @rederived row on main equal to 104, so it can never match). Hypothesis confirmed by a source the lead had not seen.
